criteria.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs (run with `cargo test -p athena-core baseline`) gives a green CI result for the base's fingerprint. `take_baseline` returns a baseline marked reused, whose checks are marked reused and pass, and the local check executor was never invoked.
criteria.evidence: Two new whole-job tests run through `Athena::go`, and both passed when I ran them. The first is `baseline_reused_from_the_landed_candidates_run_runs_nothing_locally`: its squash carries a real `Verification` whose fingerprint equals the base's, and the fake answers green only for PREVIOUS_CANDIDATE on athena/ci/<prev job>. The second is `baseline_reused_from_the_default_branch_run_runs_nothing_locally`: origin/HEAD points at origin/main and the fake answers green only for the content commit on main. Both assert that the stored baseline.json has `reused_from == Some(CI_RUN_ADDRESS)` and `note == None`, that the checks are fmt, clippy and test, each `reused && passed`, and that the reuse line is printed. They also assert that the `baseline-ran` mark left by the local check command (`touch ../../baseline-ran`) does not exist, so the local executor never ran. The landed test also asserts exactly one baseline read, on the previous candidate's SHA and CI branch. The debug-profile `cargo test -p athena-core baseline_` did not compile in this snapshot: a stale athena-data unit in the shared target dir lacked the field, although the tree is clean and records.rs:2625 has it. So I ran the same filter in the release profile. Athena's 'fails without the fix' run shows these tests do not compile without the change.

criteria.criterion: A new test (run with `cargo test -p athena-core baseline`) has no CI result, a red one, or a lookup error for the base's fingerprint. `take_baseline` runs the checks locally as before and returns the same records as before, with no reuse marker, and a red or error case also leaves a note.
criteria.evidence: `baseline_runs_locally_when_no_green_ci_result_exists` passed. It loops over seven cases: no run, a red run, an unfinished run, an unreachable host (the new `CiReply::Unreachable`, where the runner returns Err), a different fingerprint, a landing that edited a workflow, and a landing of two jobs. For each it asserts `baseline_ran`, `reused_from == None`, `note == None`, the checks fmt, clippy and test each with `reused == false`, and exactly one `ci         baseline runs locally: ` line containing the case's reason. The red case's reason names the run address. A no-origin control asserts a local run, no baseline reads and no baseline line. The 'note' for red and error cases is this printed line, not the record's `note` field, which stays None so the record is unchanged. That matches the accepted plan. The existing `a_fake_job_takes_its_baseline_before_the_producer...` test also passed.

criteria.criterion: The `Baseline` round-trip tests in crates/athena-data/src/records.rs, via `check_record_file` and `AnyRecord::Baseline` on `{job}/baseline.json`, pass with and without the new reuse field. An older baseline file with no such field still parses (`cargo test -p athena-data`).
criteria.evidence: All 8 tests passed. The new `a_baseline_written_before_reuse_existed_still_parses_with_no_source` serializes a None baseline, asserts the JSON has no `reused_from` key (the old file form), and asserts `check_record_file` accepts it on `{job}/baseline.json`, it parses with `reused_from == None`, and it validates. `a_reused_baseline_round_trips_and_validates` round-trips `Some(..)` through `AnyRecord::parse` and `check_record_file` and asserts `failed_before` excuses nothing. `a_baseline_with_an_unknown_key_is_still_refused` asserts that `deny_unknown_fields` still holds. The field is `#[serde(default, skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")]`.

criteria.criterion: `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` pass on the whole workspace.
criteria.evidence: Athena's recorded checks for 90e41dd57eec all passed, reused from CI run https://github.com/doodla/athena/actions/runs/41840183569 (fmt success, clippy success, test success). I did not rerun the full suite. I did run `cargo test --release -p athena-core ci_reuse` to check the candidate reuse path: all 7 passed, plus the refusal_corpus case.

criteria.criterion: Reuse is keyed on the same governed-content fingerprint that candidate check reuse uses, through the existing `ci_result::resolve` path, not a new lookup. The reuse decision and its reason (reused from which run, or why it ran locally) are printed in the job's output like the existing `ci         checks reused from ...` line.
criteria.evidence: From reading run/checks.rs: `reused_baseline` computes `own = fingerprint(&self.git, base, base)`, the call candidate.rs uses for base_fingerprint. It compares `own` with the landed job's `verified_fingerprint`, and with the content commit's own fingerprint before the default-branch lookup. `green_run` calls `crate::routing::run_routed_with_record` (which calls `ci_result::resolve`) inside the new `with_ci_source_on`, which is the old `with_ci_source` body with the branch made a parameter. ci_result.rs gains only a module-doc paragraph, not a new lookup function. `take_baseline` prints `ci         baseline reused from {address} for {base}` or `ci         baseline runs locally: {reason}`, and the criterion 1 and 2 tests assert both lines.

criteria.criterion: Docs or CHANGELOG.md state that the baseline can now be reused from a green CI result, and what happens when none exists.
criteria.evidence: From reading the diff: the new CHANGELOG.md Unreleased/Added entry says the baseline is reused from a green GitHub run. It names the two lookups (the landed candidate's run matched by fingerprint with no workflow edit, then the default branch's run from origin/HEAD), the `reused_from` field and the printed line. It says that otherwise (no run, unfinished, red or untrusted run, unreachable host, different fingerprint, multi-job landing, no origin/HEAD, no GitHub origin) the baseline runs locally as before with a `runs locally: <reason>` line, and that a lookup never fails the job. These claims match the code in run/checks.rs.

findings.summary: Two changed files are outside the expected deliverables list: crates/athena-core/src/checks.rs and crates/athena-core/src/reconcile.rs.
findings.evidence: `git diff HEAD~1 --stat` lists both files, and neither is in the brief's deliverables. Both were in the planned files, and both are minimal: checks.rs adds `reused_from: None` to a test `Baseline` literal, which compilation requires; reconcile.rs makes `local_default_branch` pub(crate) so it can be reused. Neither adds behavior or scope.

findings.summary: When the configured checks include more than fmt, clippy and test, a green CI run is reported as 'did not pass', which is misleading.
findings.evidence: `run_routed_with_record` marks a configured check the CI record does not name as `passed: false` ('no CI result for this check'). `green_run` then takes the `Ok((_, Some(record)))` arm and prints `the CI run <addr> for <sha> did not pass`, even though the run was green. The outcome is safe (the baseline runs locally), but the reason line is wrong. A reason such as 'the CI run does not cover check X' would be accurate.

findings.summary: Using a refusing executor to stop `run_routed_with_record` from running locally works, but it lumps every error into 'no usable CI result'.
findings.evidence: `RefuseExec::exec` bails, and `green_run` maps any `Err(_)` from routing to `no usable CI result for <sha> on <branch>` (or the workflow message). This keeps the existing resolve path as the criterion requires and is safe, because every Err means a local run. But any other routing error gets the same reason as a missing run.

findings.summary: Snapshot environment only: the debug-profile `cargo test -p athena-core baseline_` failed to compile here because of a stale athena-data unit in the shared target directory, not because of the candidate.
findings.evidence: `git status --short` is empty, and records.rs:2625 has `pub reused_from`, yet the athena-core lib build reported 'no field named reused_from' twice. Rebuilding the athena-data test unit did not refresh the lib unit. The likely cause is the earlier 'fails without the fix' revert build sharing CARGO_TARGET_DIR. The same filter in a fresh release profile (`cargo test --release -p athena-core baseline_`) compiled and passed 10 of 10. Athena's CI record for this commit shows the full test suite green. This affects the verification snapshot's target dir only, not the real repository.

summary: The change does what was asked. Before the baseline runs, `take_baseline` now looks for a green GitHub run with the same governed content as the base, using the existing `routing::run_routed_with_record` → `ci_result::resolve` path. It checks two places: the landed job's candidate run, accepted only when the `verified_fingerprint` in that job's `verification.json` equals `fingerprint(base, base)` and the landing edited no workflow file; then the default branch's push run for the base's content commit. On a hit, `baseline.json` records `reused_from`, all checks are marked reused and passed, nothing runs on this machine, and the job prints `ci         baseline reused from <run> for <base>`. When there is no hit (no run, a red or unfinished run, an unreachable host, a different fingerprint, a workflow edit, a landing of two jobs), the baseline runs here as before and a `ci         baseline runs locally: <reason>` line says why. When there is no GitHub origin it prints nothing. I ran the new tests in the snapshot and they pass: `cargo test -p athena-data baseline` (8 passed), `cargo test --release -p athena-core baseline_` (10 passed, including the three new whole-job tests) and `cargo test --release -p athena-core ci_reuse` (all pass, so candidate reuse is unchanged). fmt, clippy and the full suite are green in Athena's recorded CI run. The plain debug command `cargo test -p athena-core baseline_` failed to compile in this snapshot. The cause is a stale athena-data build in the shared target directory, not the candidate: the tree is clean and the field is present. That is why I ran the release profile. The remaining findings are minor: two changed files are not on the deliverables list, and one fallback reason can be misleading.
